frontier: OEIS A385316: smallest N = sum of 3 prime cubes (p³+q³+r³, unordered p≤q≤r) in exactly n ways — does the claimed multiplicity-3 and multiplicity-6 values actually exist under complete-prime-set enumeration?

Independent enumeration confirms 0 sums with multiplicity ≥ 2 at C=100,000. Prior session's claim of "5 multiplicity-3 values at C=5×10⁷" is incompatible with this reproducible result under identical problem specification (complete prime set, unordered triplets, p≤q≤r).
result: Negative result: under the complete-prime-set, unordered-enumeration interpretation, OEIS A385316 terms for n≥2 either do not exist through C=100,000 or the OEIS definition uses a different enumeration rule (e.g., ordered triplets, different prime-set cutoff, or allowing repeated primes with order significance). Prior session's accepted continuation citing "5 multiplicity-3 values" cannot be reproduced with the stated problem definition. The route to a(6) under this interpretation requires either: (a) confirming the correct OEIS enumeration convention, or (b) proving that multiplicity-n sums exist beyond a much higher threshold.
next_gate: Verify the exact OEIS A385316 problem statement — check whether it requires ordered triplets (p,q,r) with p,q,r distinct, or allows any ordering, or uses a different summand set (e.g., prime powers instead of primes). Once confirmed, rewrite the enumerator to match the canonical definition and re-run the multiplicity census.
